svg.title: A toolbox release collides with a file I hand-edited — the update shows the conflict — a toolbox update collides with my edit on a framework file, and I resolve it
svg.text: A toolbox release collides with a file I hand-edited —
Scenario: a toolbox update collides with my edit on a framework file, and I resolve it
My edit and the release collide on the same line
I resolve the conflict and keep my intent

g.text: Given a project generated from an earlier toolbox release pins its CI
image to that release
A project made from an older toolbox release (1.0.0). Its CI pipeline runs inside a toolbox
image, pinned to that release — the line on screen is the image every pipeline run uses.
This .gitlab-ci.yml is framework-owned, so an update is allowed to change it.
When the developer hand-edits that framework file and commits the
change
The team pins their own hardened image tag on that same line and commits it. Because
.gitlab-ci.yml is framework-owned, the next toolbox update will try to change this very line
too.
When a newer release moves the same line and the developer runs the
toolbox update
The exact command Renovate runs on its own for a new release. This release (1.0.1) moves the
image to the new toolbox version — the same line the developer just changed.
Then the update keeps the new line and saves my change in a reject file
The update can't merge two different edits to the same line. It keeps the new release's line
in .gitlab-ci.yml and saves the developer's change in a .gitlab-ci.yml.rej file — a patch to
reapply by hand. Nothing is silently dropped.
When the developer resolves the conflict and keeps their pin on the new
release
The developer keeps their hardening intent, now on top of the new release: the image becomes
:1.0.1-hardened. The conflict marks are removed and the fix is staged.
Then the tree is clean again and the developer's own intent is
preserved
After committing the resolution the working tree is clean, the update is complete, and the
image line carries the developer's hardening applied to the new toolbox release.
